newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Cocoa may drift lower after Tuesday's rout.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Cocoa may drift lower after Tuesday's rout.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

LIFFE July cocoa futures are likely to drift sideways and possibly move lower to the 960 stg area seen in February after Tuesday's fall to the lowest level in more than two weeks, analysts said on Wednesday.
Traders called the market to open unchanged.
Susan Rigg, an analyst at Chart Analysis, said cocoa had seen its immediate peak at the end-March and early-April level of 1,060 stg.
Further progress was impeded by layers of resistance above that area.
She said that after Tuesday's fall cocoa was likely to come back to the April reaction lows of 980 stg.

"We should test it but there's some hesitation in the near term. However, the upward progress has been routed on the particular (Tuesday's move) and I think the market would now move in a sideways range."
Rigg added that a break lower to 960 was also possible.
On the fundamental side, broker GNI sharply cut its 1996/97 world cocoa deficit estimate to 33,000 tonnes from its earlier forecast of 180,000 tonnes.
It raised its production forecast to reflect the higher Ivorian crop estimate.
"We would not even rule out a marginal supply surplus if the (Ivorian) mid-crop comes in as large as some traders are predicting," GNI said in a daily commentary.
Local Ivorian analysts put the mid-crop (May-Sept) at 180,000 tonnes but that figure could be revised in June depending on rainfall.
GNI put total Ivorian output at 1.15 million, including a mid-crop of 160,000. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
